dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: Oh Archons, I'm out of my depth... We're understaffed and undersupplied, and I can't even treat half of the wounds I'm seeing...

dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: I just wish I had someone with more expertise to turn to... Ugh, no, I mustn't think like that. I have to rise to the challenge!

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: I saw you brought Chuychu back... It's such a tragedy. Chuychu was the most promising doctor I ever had the pleasure to meet.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: We were close business partners. She had the highest standards for medical supplies, and she'd often dip into her own pockets to treat her patients.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: She always told me how she valued the experience more than the money.

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: She said she had to perfect her skills so that she could save more people, especially the one person she wanted to save the most...

dialogues.speaker: Awhina
dialogues.text: Sadly, in the end, the one person she couldn't save was herself. And now Natlan has lost one of the finest talents of a generation...

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: What's the status? Do we have enough medical supplies left?

dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: We're almost out. There are still the emergency supplies, but they're reserved for the doctors and soldiers. We can't touch those.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: I know, I know...

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Alright, well... give me my share, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: What's the status? Do we have enough medical supplies left?

dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: We're almost out. There are still the emergency supplies, but they're reserved for the doctors and soldiers. We can't touch those.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: I know, I know...

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Alright, well... give me my share, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Glad to see you're both alright.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your son doing?

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: No idea. Communications have dried up, and there are too many wounded people to attend to. Right now, my focus is on them.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: But I trust him. I know he'll make the right call even when the going gets tough. He's my son, and I'll always be proud of him.

dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: I'm so grateful Mayahuel is here. With her expertise, we were able to treat a lot more people.

dialogues.speaker: Qhispe
dialogues.text: But I'm worried she's overdoing it. She hasn't stopped this whole time. I need to get someone else to step in so I can persuade her to take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: I trust him. I know he'll make the right call even when the going gets tough. He's my son, and I'll always be proud of him.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: It's you two! Fantastic! I'm so grateful for all your encouragement.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: So many people in Natlan see it as an honor to fight the Abyss, but then they let the excitement get to their heads and end up putting themselves in great danger.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: You were right: It's important to fight, but it's also important to stay alive. We fight for the people we love, and also for the chance to see them again.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: I shared your thoughts with my brothers-in-arms, and they were inspired too. Now everyone's fighting with more determination, and we're turning the tide!

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: So once again... thank you from the bottom of my heart!

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: ...Oh, it's you two. I thought we'd never see each other again.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: I put up a good fight, and we won, even though it cost us dearly...

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Are you gonna keep fighting? If so, please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Uturunku
dialogues.text: Fighting the Abyss is a great honor, but the path to victory lies not in honor and glory, but in surviving until the next morning.

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. Thank you for saving me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're just glad you're okay. Hey, where did those saurians go?

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: Oh, they're back at it again, helping the remaining messengers with scouting and intel delivery.

dialogues.speaker: Raman
dialogues.text: It kills me, not being able to do my part. Especially knowing how bad things have gotten out there. But, you gotta know your limits, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Iyoba
dialogues.text: Oh, hey you guys. Thanks again for rescuing us. Osawe, look who it is! Say "thank-you" to these heroes!

dialogues.speaker: Osawe
dialogues.text: Thank you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, don't mention it. Just glad you're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Osawe
dialogues.text: I also gotta say thank-you to the other people who helped us. What were they called? Fat... chewy...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fatui!

dialogues.speaker: Osawe
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's it, the Fatui! They were also amazing...

dialogues.speaker: Iyoba
dialogues.text: Yeah. In the past, my impression of the Fatui wasn't exactly positive, but this has really changed my perspective. Good people can be found in every organization.

dialogues.speaker: Haronga
dialogues.text: The saurians I came back with were intent on following the other warriors into battle. There was just nothing I could do to stop them.

dialogues.speaker: Haronga
dialogues.text: That officially makes me the most useless member of the unit... *sigh* But at least I know enough about saurian medicine to help treat their injuries.

dialogues.speaker: Young Yumkasaur
dialogues.text: Roar ♪

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, it's the yumkasaur we rescued! You made it back! Aww, that's such good news...

dialogues.speaker: Young Yumkasaur
dialogues.text: Roar, roar!

dialogues.speaker: Libiac
dialogues.text: I'm delighted to see you make it back safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just keeping our word! We said we'd see you at the stadium.

dialogues.speaker: Kunak
dialogues.text: Heh... Y'know, this was the first time in my life slaying an Abyss monster, and I realized in that moment... they're not that tough.

dialogues.speaker: Kunak
dialogues.text: I let my fear win for too long... Makes me wonder how many people I could've saved if I'd just had the courage.

dialogues.speaker: Libiac
dialogues.text: Don't be so hard on yourself. Right now, staying alive is the most important thing you can do. We must live on so their stories can be told.

dialogues.speaker: Libiac
dialogues.text: They will live forever in our hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Achiyaku
dialogues.text: You're okay! Thank goodness, we were worried sick about you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you made it to safety, huh? Was it a smooth journey?

dialogues.speaker: Achiyaku
dialogues.text: Uh... not exactly. We ran into a bunch of Abyss monsters and had to fight for our lives. But I gotta hand it to these folks, they really rose to the occasion. They fought every bit as well as trained warriors.

dialogues.speaker: Libiac
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess the old muscle memory's still intact!

dialogues.speaker: Kunak
dialogues.text: I feel very lucky to be alive. We have to keep surviving, so we can start to take back what we've lost.

dialogues.speaker: Kunak
dialogues.text: You guys better make sure you keep surviving too.

dialogues.speaker: Mayahuel
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Glad to see you're both alright.
